experiment: N4kd with ALPHA=1.0 (hard labels), 5-fold subject-level CV
finding: The original 16-subject validation split sits BELOW all five folds (0.6763 vs fold range 0.6917-0.7426). It was a pessimistic draw, so every 'bar to beat' in this project was set against a harder-than-average yardstick.
practical_bar: Believe a change if it moves the CV mean by more than one across-fold sd (0.0193 kappa).
caveat: The sd is a descriptive spread, not a standard error. Folds share training data; there is no unbiased estimator of k-fold CV variance.

correlations_withheld.why: Fold-level correlates of kappa were computed and are NOT reported as findings. ST subject count takes only 2 distinct values across 5 folds (one fold has 3, four have 4), so any correlation with it is a two-group comparison with n=1 in one group. It also points opposite to the measured cohort effect (ST scores 0.106 below SC), which suggests noise. n=5 cannot apportion fold variance between cohort mix, subject difficulty and initialisation.
